order: say if someone's face or breathing has changed

little.skill: Hello dog, bees and farm animals
little.twist: Nothing glows when you say hello to the dog, and you choose the way past the horse by yourself.
little.can_now: ask before stroking a dog, be a tree when a dog runs at them, walk away from bees and keep away from behind a horse

steps.say: The practice park. Animals have feelings too. Let's learn to be safe and kind with them.
A lady is walking her dog, Biscuit. You'd love to stroke him. What do you do first?

choices.text: Ask the owner if I may

choices.why: Dogs can be scared by a hug from someone they don't know. Ask the owner first.

steps.done: The lady says yes: he's friendly.

steps.say: Let Biscuit sniff the back of your hand. Hold it out, low and still.
steps.done: Sniff, sniff: now he knows you.

steps.say: Say hello the dog's way: what does Biscuit sniff first?
steps.done: The back of your hand, low and still.

not.dog_head: Not on top of the head: most dogs like a gentle stroke on the side or the back.

steps.say: Now stroke his side gently.
steps.done: His tail wags softly: he likes that.

not.dog_head: Not on top of the head: most dogs like a gentle stroke on the side or the back.

steps.say: Where do dogs like a gentle stroke?
steps.done: On the side: you knew by yourself.

steps.say: Another dog is fast asleep under the bench.

choices.why: A dog that is sleeping or eating wants to be left alone.

steps.done: Let sleeping dogs sleep: and eating ones eat.

steps.say: If a dog ever runs at you: be a tree. Stand still, fold your arms in, and look at your feet. Never run.
Here comes a dog without its owner. Be a tree!
steps.done: It sniffs, gets bored and trots back to its owner. Well done for keeping still!

steps.say: A bee buzzes round your picnic.

choices.why: Swatting can make it sting. Walk away slowly and calmly.

steps.done: Slowly and calmly: the bee goes back to the flowers.

steps.say: Ouch! A bee stung Bobo's arm. What do you do?

choices.why: Always tell a grown-up about a sting: they know how to help.

steps.done: A grown-up helps. A sting hurts, then it gets better.

not.horse_back: Never walk behind a horse: it can't see you there and might kick.

steps.say: On the farm: walk past the horse the safe way.
steps.done: At its side, where it can see you.

not.horse_back: Never walk behind a horse: it can't see you there and might kick.

steps.say: Which way past the horse?
steps.done: Where it can see you: all by yourself.

steps.say: Ask first, the back of your hand, be a tree, walk away from bees, and never behind a horse!

check.say: You want to stroke a dog you don't know. First...
A dog runs at you. You...

choices.text: Be a tree: still, arms in

check.say: A bee buzzes near you. You...

name_it.title: Ask, sniff, be a tree
lines: Ask the owner first, then let the dog sniff the back of your hand.
Leave dogs alone when they eat or sleep.
A dog runs at you: be a tree. Still, arms in, look at your feet.
Walk away slowly from bees and wasps; never behind a horse.
name_it.source: The Dogs Trust's Be Dog Smart, Doggone Safe's Be a Tree, the Kennel Club and the RSPCA

little.try_real: Next time you meet a dog with its owner, show your grown-up how you ask first and hold out the back of your hand. Practise being a tree together at home.

sources.fact: Always ask the owner before stroking a dog; let it sniff the back of your hand; stroke it gently on the side or back.
If a dog runs at you, 'be a tree': stand still, fold your arms in and look at your feet; don't run, shout or stare; walk away slowly once it goes, and tell a grown-up.
sources.source: Doggone Safe's Be a Tree programme; the Kennel Club, how to behave safely around dogs

sources.fact: Leave dogs alone while they are eating or sleeping.
Don't swat at bees or wasps: move away calmly; never walk behind a horse.
sources.source: NHS, insect bites and stings; the British Horse Society

middle.skill: Dog signs, be a tree, farm and wild
middle.twist: The three dogs stand in new places, and nothing glows when you say hello.
middle.can_now: read a dog's warning signs, greet a dog safely, be a tree when a dog runs at them, and stay safe near farm animals, wasps and snakes

steps.say: The practice park, a farm and a hill path. Today: how dogs talk with their bodies, saying hello, a dog running at you, cows, wasps and snakes.

not.dog_relaxed: This dog is relaxed: a loose body, a soft face, a gently wagging tail.
not.dog_play: Bottom up, front legs down: a play bow. This dog wants to play.

steps.say: Three dogs. One is saying 'leave me alone'. Which one?
steps.done: Yes: a stiff body, a hard stare, lips pulled back and a tail held high and stiff.

not.dog_relaxed: This dog is relaxed: a loose body, a soft face, a gently wagging tail.
not.dog_play: Bottom up, front legs down: a play bow. This dog wants to play.

steps.say: Which dog is saying 'leave me alone'?
steps.done: You read it by yourself: stiff, staring, lips back, tail high.

lines.sign_tail: The tail held high and stiff.

steps.say: Find its four warning signs.
steps.done: Give a dog like that lots of space, and walk away slowly.

safe_mistake.wrong: hugging a dog you don't know
safe_mistake.why: Most dogs don't like hugs: arms round the neck feel like being trapped, and a worried dog may snap.
safe_mistake.right: Ask the owner first, let it sniff the back of your hand, then stroke its side gently.

steps.say: A friendly-looking dog you don't know is with its owner. You want to say hello. What do you do?
steps.done: The owner says yes: Biscuit loves a gentle stroke.

steps.say: Let him sniff the back of your hand: low and still.
steps.done: Now he knows you.

not.dog_head: Not on top of the head: most dogs like a gentle stroke on the side or the back.

steps.say: Stroke his side gently.
steps.done: A soft, wagging tail.

steps.say: Back in the park, a dog without its owner comes running towards you.

safe_mistake.why: Running makes a dog want to chase you, like a game.
safe_mistake.right: Be a tree: stand still, fold your arms in and look at your feet. The dog gets bored and goes.

steps.say: What do you do?
steps.done: Still as a tree: it sniffs, gets bored and trots off. Then walk away slowly.

not.horse_back: Never walk behind a horse: it can't see you there and might kick.

steps.say: The farm. Walk past the horse the safe way.
steps.done: At its side, talking softly so it knows you are there.

steps.say: Your path goes through a field of cows with their calves.

choices.text: Walk calmly round the edge, away from the calves

choices.why: Cows protect their calves: running near them or between them can upset them. Walk calmly round the edge.

steps.done: Calm and slow, round the edge, and close the gate behind you.

steps.say: At your picnic, a wasp lands on your sandwich.

choices.text: Stay calm and move away slowly

choices.why: Swatting can make a wasp sting. Move away slowly, and cover drinks outside.

steps.done: No swatting: it flies off.

steps.say: Pip-pop is stung. Then her lips swell, and her breathing sounds strange.

choices.text: Get a grown-up and call {number}: it's an emergency

choices.why: A swollen face or trouble breathing after a sting is an allergy emergency: call {number} straight away.

steps.done: An allergy after a sting is an emergency: help comes fast.

not.snake: Never touch or poke a snake: leave it alone.

steps.say: On the hill path, a snake lies in the sun. What do you do?
steps.done: Step back slowly and give it space: it will move away. Then go round, far from it.

steps.say: Read the signs, ask first, be a tree, calm round cows, no swatting, and leave snakes alone. Animals need their space!

check.say: A dog that says 'leave me alone' has...

choices.text: A stiff body and a hard stare

check.say: A dog you don't know. You want to hug it. You...

choices.text: Ask the owner, then stroke its side

check.say: A dog runs at you. You...
A snake lies on the path. You...

choices.text: Step back slowly and go round

name_it.title: Read the dog, be a tree
lines: Warning signs: a stiff body, a hard stare, lips back, the tail high. Give it space.
Ask the owner, let it sniff your hand, stroke its side: no hugs.
A dog runs at you: be a tree. Running makes it chase.
Calm round cows and horses, no swatting wasps, and leave snakes alone.
name_it.source: The Dogs Trust, the Kennel Club, the RSPCA, the Countryside Code, and the NHS (stings)

middle.try_real: With a grown-up, watch dogs in the park from far away: which ones are relaxed, which want space? Practise being a tree, and talk about what to do after a sting.

sources.fact: Warning signs in a dog include a stiff body, staring, lips pulled back, a raised tail and growling: give the dog space and move away slowly.
sources.source: Dogs Trust, Be Dog Smart; the RSPCA

sources.fact: Most dogs don't like being hugged; ask the owner, let the dog sniff the back of your hand, stroke the side or back.
sources.source: The Kennel Club, Safe and Sound

sources.fact: If a dog runs at you, don't run: be a tree (still, arms folded in, look at your feet); dogs react to running, noise and staring.
sources.source: Doggone Safe's Be a Tree programme; the Blue Dog programme's guidance (as text)

sources.fact: Around cows, especially with calves, walk calmly round the edge of the field and keep away; never walk behind a horse.
Call 999 or 112 if someone has a swollen face, mouth or throat or trouble breathing after a sting: it can be anaphylaxis.
If you see a snake, keep away and leave it alone; most bites happen when people try to touch or catch one.

big.skill: The hills, guard dogs and stings
big.twist: The guard dog comes from the other side, and nothing glows past the flock.
big.can_now: walk in the hills with their group, keep away from wild animals and guard dogs, and act fast when a sting causes an allergy

steps.say: The practice hills: a walk with your group. {wild_where}
Your group walks on the path. You'd like to look at some flowers far off it.

choices.text: Stay with the group, on the path

choices.why: Stay with your group and the grown-ups: never wander off alone in the hills.

steps.done: Together, on the path.

steps.say: Make some noise as you walk, so animals hear you coming and move away: clap three times.
steps.done: Wild animals usually keep away from people they can hear coming.

steps.say: Far across the valley: a bear! It hasn't seen you.

choices.text: Stop, stay together and go back slowly the way you came

choices.why: Running can make an animal chase. Go back slowly and calmly, together.
Never go closer to a wild animal, or follow it: give it lots of space.

steps.done: Slowly back the way you came, all together.

steps.say: At your picnic spot, a fox comes close, looking at your food.

choices.text: Never feed it: pack the food away

choices.why: Wild animals that are fed come back for more and can bite. Never feed or touch them.

steps.done: Food packed away: the fox wanders off.

steps.say: A flock of sheep on the hillside, guarded by big shepherd dogs. Their job is to keep the sheep safe.

not.flock_near: Too close to the flock: the dogs guard their sheep. Go round, far away.

steps.say: Which way do you go past the flock?
steps.done: Far round it, slowly, without staring at the dogs.

not.flock_near: Too close to the flock: the dogs guard their sheep. Go round, far away.

steps.say: Which way past the flock?
steps.done: Far round it: you chose by yourself.

safe_mistake.why: Running makes a dog chase. A guard dog only wants you away from its sheep.
safe_mistake.right: Be a tree: still, arms folded in, eyes down. Then back away slowly, far from the flock.

steps.say: One of the dogs runs towards you. What do you do?
steps.done: Still as a tree: the dog sees you aren't after its sheep, and goes back.

safe_mistake.why: Running makes a dog chase. A guard dog only wants you away from its sheep.
safe_mistake.right: Be a tree: still, arms folded in, eyes down. Then back away slowly, far from the flock.

steps.say: A dog runs at you from the other side. What do you do?
steps.done: A tree, all by yourself: it goes back to its sheep.

steps.say: Now back away slowly, keeping well away from the flock.
steps.done: Slowly away. A shepherd waves: thank you for going round.

not.snake: Never touch, poke or pick up a snake: leave it alone.

steps.say: A snake lies across the path in the sun.
steps.done: Step back slowly: it will move away. If someone is ever bitten: keep them still and calm, and call {number}.

steps.say: Back at the picnic, Mo is stung by a wasp. Her face and lips swell, and her breathing sounds noisy: an allergic reaction.
It's an emergency. Pick up the phone and call {number}.
steps.done: Phone in your hand.

steps.say: Press {number}: {number_words}.
steps.done: Calling. Say 'anaphylaxis', and where you are.

steps.say: Mo carries her own auto-injector pen. What happens now?

choices.text: A grown-up, or Mo herself, uses her pen
Wait for her to feel better
choices.why: In an allergy emergency every minute matters: her own pen, and {number}.

steps.done: Gus helps Mo use her pen, and the ambulance is coming. You can practise the pen in Medical Emergencies.

steps.say: Stay together, make noise, never feed or follow wild animals, go round flocks, be a tree, and act fast after a sting. Expert walker!

choices.text: Stay with the group on the path

check.say: A wild animal far away. You...
A guard dog runs at you. You...

choices.text: Be a tree, then back away slowly

check.say: After a sting, a face swells. You...

name_it.title: Together, noisy, far away
lines: Stay with your group on the path, and make some noise as you walk.
Never feed, follow or go closer to a wild animal.
Go far round flocks; a guard dog runs at you: be a tree, then back away slowly.
A swollen face or noisy breathing after a sting: call {number}, and their own pen.
name_it.source: Mountain Rescue, the Countryside Code, the Dogs Trust, and Anaphylaxis UK and the NHS

big.try_real: Plan a walk in the hills with your grown-ups: who stays with whom, what to do if you see a big animal or a flock, and what's in the first aid kit.

sources.fact: Stay with your group; make noise on the path so animals hear you coming; never approach, feed or follow wild animals.
sources.source: US National Park Service, bear safety; Mountain Rescue England and Wales

sources.fact: Livestock guardian dogs protect flocks: keep well away from the flock, walk round it slowly, don't stare at or run from the dogs.
sources.source: The Countryside Code; European livestock guardian dog guidance for walkers

sources.fact: In Georgia's Greater Caucasus live brown bears, wolves and wild boar; Caucasian shepherd dogs guard flocks in the mountains.
Anaphylaxis signs include swelling of the face, lips or throat and breathing difficulty: call 999 or 112, use the person's own adrenaline auto-injector if they have one.
If someone is bitten by a snake: keep them still and calm and get medical help straight away; don't try to catch the snake.
